summary.offshore_note: loitering ships < 60 nm, < 3 kn, at large-container-ship hotelling loads. Valid for the 2021-22 backlog (mostly queued container ships); in normal times these slow ships are a mixed fleet, so do not headline the offshore number for 2024
summary.method: POLA Inventory of Air Emissions 2023: anchorage hotelling loads (Tables 3.2, 3.5) x 0.1% S MGO emission factors (Tables 3.12, 3.13); ship-hours at anchor from AIS
summary.scope: every cargo ship and tanker anchored in San Pedro Bay (both ports, plus refinery/crude tankers and ships waiting on orders), not only POLA calls

pola_2023_inventory.source: POLA Inventory of Air Emissions CY2023, Tables 3.7 and 3.16 (hotelling at-anchorage)

pola_2021_inventory.source: POLA Inventory of Air Emissions CY2021, Table 3.16 (hotelling at-anchorage)

cross_check.note: our rate per ship-day is about half POLA's implied rate (conservative); our ship-days are higher because POLA counts only its own calls

carb.source: CARB, Emissions Impact of Ships Anchored at POLA/POLB (Nov 2021); Emissions Impacts of Vessel Congestion ... February 2023 Update (Table 1, Fig. 2)
